transcript.text: Hi there! I'd love to chat and get to know you a bit. To kick things off, tell me about the last time you were around a lot of people for a long time. How did you feel afterwards?

Oh, wow, last weekend I ended up at this giant neighborhood block party that just went on for hours! Honestly, I was totally buzzing with so much wonderful energy from meeting all these fascinating new folks and hearing their wild travel stories. By the time I finally got home, my feet hurt from dancing, but my heart was so full—though I definitely needed to crash on the couch with some tea right after!

It sounds like those new stories really sparked your imagination! When your mind wanders and nothing demands your attention, what kind of ideas or thoughts do you usually find yourself drifting toward?

Oh, totally! My mind goes a million miles an hour, usually dreaming up some wild new creative project—like last week I randomly decided I need to learn how to weave my own tapestries, or maybe build a fairy garden in the backyard. I just love chasing those sudden sparks of inspiration and wondering, "Ooh, what if I tried *that*?"
I love that endless curiosity! Tell me about a time you had to give someone feedback or news they wouldn't like. What went through your mind, and what did you actually do?

Oh gosh, that's always the absolute worst part—my stomach just twists into knots because I hate hurting anyone's feelings! When I had to tell my friend Sarah that I couldn't help her move this weekend because I promised to help plant a community garden instead, I ended up rambling and practically crying apologies before I even got the words out. I just wanted to make sure she knew how much I adore her while still staying true to what feels right in my heart!
That empathy really shines through. Walk me through how you usually handle a big trip, move, or deadline—do you map everything out well in advance, or prefer to keep things open and see how it goes?

Oh, rigid plans are basically my kryptonite—they make me feel so trapped and stressed out! I’d much rather just pack a bag on a whim, book a last-minute train ticket somewhere random, and see what kind of magical hidden cafes or lovely strangers I stumble into along the way. Who wants to follow a strict spreadsheet when the best adventures happen entirely by accident?

It sounds like you have a wonderful knack for embracing whatever life brings your way! Tell me about a time when you had to tackle a really tedious, practical task that had zero room for creativity. What did you do to get through it?

Oh, paying taxes or organizing spreadsheets is absolute torture for me—my brain just completely turns to mush! I usually blast some wildly upbeat 80s pop music, dance around the room with my cat, and bribe myself with fancy chocolate every ten minutes just to survive it.
